html:
Operation Boleas was the military intervention in Lesotho by South African and Botswana troops, under the Southern African Development Community, which began on 22 September 1998 after a disputed election.

The opposition claimed the May 1998 election was rigged, and protests and a mutiny in the army threatened the government. South African troops met unexpected resistance from the Lesotho army, and in the chaos much of central Maseru was looted and burned.

The troops left in 1999 after an agreement for new elections, held with a mixed voting system in 2002. It was the first big military operation of post-apartheid South Africa abroad, and in Lesotho it is remembered as an invasion. Troops also guarded the Katse Dam.
sum: Operation Boleas was the military intervention in Lesotho by South African and Botswana troops, under the Southern African Development Community, which began on 22 September 1998 after a disputed election.
